chief_complaint: One episode of strange sensations in the right side of her body.
history_of_present_illness: Sensations started in the right side of her face, marched to her right arm, and then continued to involve her right leg, described as 'pins and needles' lasting for about 2 minutes; a similar episode occurred several months ago without medical consultation.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Four years prior, she spent 2 years backpacking through South America (Ecuador, Peru, Argentina) and South-east Asia (Thailand, Laos, Cambodia), staying in hostels or private accommodations as an 'eco-traveller' visiting the countryside and local people. She has been a strict vegan for 8 years, eating food from local vendors (fruits, vegetables, nuts, rice) but no animal products.
physical_exam: She looks well and is afebrile; her neurological examination is completely unremarkable, and the rest of her physical examination is also normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Routine blood investigations, including differential blood count and C-reactive protein, are completely normal. CSF examination is unremarkable. MRI of her brain with gadolinium enhancement shows multiple cortical and subcortical cystic lesions in both hemispheres.
differential_diagnosis: The patient presents with a focal epileptic seizure, with paraesthesias representing a Jacksonian 'sensory march', and neuroimaging revealing multiple cortical and subcortical cystic lesions, some with gadolinium enhancement and surrounding oedema; given the presentation and travel history, the most likely diagnosis is neurocysticercosis with multiple cysts in the vesicular and colloidal stage, confirmed by positive enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot (EITB) for anticysticercal antibodies in serum and CSF.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with albendazole 400 mg bd for 10 days and started on antiepileptic drugs, but declined corticosteroids. She remained seizure-free for 1 year, with MRI showing regression of all cysts. A CT scan at 2-year follow-up showed two calcifications. Antiepileptic treatment was stopped after a seizure-free period of 3 years.
